children: Reserve management purchases were paused amid a little-changed reserve demand, a material change to the forecast for reserve supply, and signals of ample reserves from money markets, according to Roberto Perli, manager of the System Open Market Account, Federal Reserve Bank of New York.
Perli was speaking at the 2026 U.S. Treasury Market Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York City.
Last month, the New York Federal Reserve announced a temporary pause in Treasury security purchases under the RMP program.
The news comes amid Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's preference for a leaner Fed balance sheet.

"Our decisions on the size of RMPs are informed by three considerations, all equally important: our assessment of reserve demand, our forecast for reserve supply, and both current and expected money market conditions," said Perli.

"We assessed that reserve demand was little changed over that time. In contrast, our forecast for reserve supply did change materially as we updated it to reflect Treasury's guidance for the end-of-December level of the Treasury General Account, which was lower than we had previously assumed," said Perli.

"The result was a shift higher in our estimate for the supply of reserves. This upward revision to reserve supply, combined with a low likelihood of very large swings in that supply (as seen, for example, around April tax season), limited the risks that reserves might fall below ample levels later in our forecast horizon," noted Perli.

"Various signals from money markets confirmed that reserves were ample and likely to remain so in the near term," he added. "Accordingly, we felt it appropriate to reduce our RMPs to zero since mid-August."

Warsh had advocated for a smaller Fed balance sheet during his confirmation hearing, and the first thing he had the Committee do was change the language in their Implementation Notes, which are instructions to the NY Fed Open Market Desk,

What had previously stated "Increase SOMA holdings of securities through purchases of Treasury Bills" was altered to "When appropriate, increase SOMA holdings of securities through the purchase of Treasury Bills."
By adding the wording "when appropriate" the Fed was essentially ending the RMPs, unless absolutely necessary, noted Gray.

title: Reserve management purchases paused amid signals of ample reserves: SOMA's Perli
